excluded.test: actions.test.ts > actions.test.ts > entry/exit actions > when stopped > should clear all scheduled events when the interpreter gets stopped
excluded.reason: the action that handles INITIALIZE_SYNC_SEQUENCE sends its own actor two SOME_EVENTs and then stops it while that event is processed, so the stop clears the two from its mailbox and SOME_EVENT's throwing action never runs. The vocabulary can stage this only on a child: the child queues the two with send_to '#_internal' and asks its parent with send_parent to stop it, which the parent does with stop_child, the same _stop() and mailbox.clear() that root.stop() runs (createActor.ts). Measured on XState, that child processes no SOME_EVENT and ends stopped, in either order of the sends, because XState runs the child's deferred sends while the child still processes INITIALIZE_SYNC_SEQUENCE and delivers the send_parent to the idle parent at once, nested there, so the stop clears the two before the child reaches them. xactor queues every delivery in one FIFO, and a child asked to stop first handles the events that arrived before the request (doc: #xstate-invariant-a6 and #differences-interleaving), so xstate would process both SOME_EVENTs. Kept for that divergence; no action stops the root from inside a macrostep, and the stop step stops the root between steps, when its mailbox is empty

excluded.test: actions.test.ts > actions.test.ts > entry/exit actions > when stopped > should execute exit actions of the settled state of the last initiated microstep
excluded.reason: service.stop() is called from inside a transition action while INITIALIZE_SYNC_SEQUENCE is still being processed, and the test asserts which exit and transition actions still run; the core oracle runs XState's pure functions and has no actor to stop, the actor cases' stop step stops the root only between steps, and no declared action stops the actor that is running it (stop_child stops a child). It would need an action that stops its own actor while it executes
